# function: state_trigger

Returns an automation `state` trigger, for use in `triggers`. Further trigger options, e.g. `to`, `from` or `for`, go in `options`. Write `for` as a quoted key, `{ "for" = "00:05:00" }`, because HCL reads `{ for` as a `for` expression.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# State triggers; further trigger options go in an optional trailing object.
locals {
  # Same as { trigger = "state", entity_id = "binary_sensor.hall_motion", to = "on" }
  motion = provider::homeassistant::state_trigger("binary_sensor.hall_motion", { to = "on" })
  # Quote "for": HCL reads `{ for` as the start of a for expression.
  doors_open = provider::homeassistant::state_trigger(
    ["binary_sensor.front_door", "binary_sensor.back_door"],
    { "for" = { minutes = 5 }, to = "on" },
  )
}
```

## Signature

<!-- signature generated by tfplugindocs -->
```text
state_trigger(entity_id dynamic, options dynamic...) dynamic
```

## Arguments

<!-- arguments generated by tfplugindocs -->
1. `entity_id` (Dynamic) Entity ID, e.g. `binary_sensor.motion`, or a list of entity IDs.
<!-- variadic argument generated by tfplugindocs -->
1. `options` (Variadic, Dynamic) At most one object of further keys to set on the result, e.g. `{ name = "Kitchen" }`. Keys with a null value are left out. It must not set a key that another argument already sets.
